title: Manyhands JSON v1 comment mutation data
description: The data of a comment add envelope whose comment was checkpointed in its item's editing context: the comment, the synchronization that publishes it, and how far that got. The effects of the envelope say what the request wrote and committed, and what was published and merged. A request that stopped before its comment was checkpointed carries no data. It holds no body.

type.description: The one value that tells this data apart.

item_id.description: The item the comment is filed under.

parent_id.description: The comment this one replies to. Null for a root comment.

created_by.description: The comment's created_by, as its checkpoint holds it: the author the request gave, written verbatim, or else the name and email of the identity that checkpointed it, as Name <email>. Null when the checkpoint cannot be read.

synchronization_id.description: The synchronization that publishes the comment: the ID its conflict is inspected, resolved and resumed by.

publication.description: As the envelope's publication effect says: published, current when the remote already held the comment, or pending.

pending_reason.description: Why the publication is pending, set exactly when it is: no_publication_remote for a repository with none, where a later item sync publishes the comment; recovery_required when the comment's own index hand-off, or the proof of its checkpoint, is to be done first; synchronization when its synchronization stopped, as the envelope's code says.

conflict.description: The next step of the conflict the synchronization stopped on, in a merge of its own left in the item's editing worktree. Null when it stopped on none. It names no path and holds no content.

operation_id.description: The synchronization the conflict is of: synchronization_id.

next_action.description: resolve when every conflicted path is canonical content of one item, which can be resolved in Manyhands; external_repair when any is not, so the merge is finished in Git outside Manyhands.
